title: Circular-Economy and Sustainable-AI Assessment
primary_chapter_title: Circular Health Systems and Resource Stewardship
purpose: Apply the circularity hierarchy from prevention and reduction through sharing, maintenance, reuse, refurbishment, recovery, and disposal.

records.Decision question and evidence: Can the service need be met without new acquisition, unnecessary computation, duplicate data, or low-value activity?
Can model, storage, data, hardware, energy, water, and material intensity be reduced per useful output?
Can infrastructure, services, capacity, or assets be shared without unacceptable dependency or access effects?
Can preventive maintenance, software support, components, and repair preserve safe useful life?
Can the asset or component serve a verified use after data erasure, validation, and recipient due diligence?
Can selected components and controls restore performance and evidence at lower lifecycle burden?
Are take-back, traceability, verified recovery, and critical-material outcomes documented?
Is final disposal necessary, lawful, secure, and supported by chain of custody?
Could lower unit cost or greater capacity increase total use or shift burden across places, groups, or lifecycle stages?
